name: Waveshare JetRacer
description: A pre-assembled hardware kit built to run NVIDIA's own open-source JetRacer software — Ackermann front-steering, a Jetson Nano carrier board, and a CSI camera, with GPU-accelerated TensorRT road-following out of the box. This is the base "JetRacer AI Kit"; Waveshare also sells a faster Pro variant and a ROS-equipped Professional kit with lidar and an IMU. Every SKU runs exclusively on the Jetson Nano, which NVIDIA is now discontinuing — a real caveat worth knowing before buying.

sourcing: Verified against Waveshare's official JetRacer AI Kit, Pro AI Kit, and ROS AI Kit product pages and wiki; the original NVIDIA-AI-IOT/jetracer GitHub repository and Waveshare's own fork; NVIDIA's blog and Hackster's coverage of Jetson Nano cars at DIY Robocars events; NVIDIA developer-forum threads confirming both the Jetson Nano Developer Kit's discontinuation and community use of this specific hardware; Tianbot's separate same-named project (for the naming-disambiguation note); and Amazon/AliExpress/RobotShop listings for pricing and bundle-configuration variance. Flagged as uncertain: exact current DIY Robocars league activity level for Nano-class hardware in 2026 (historical evidence is solid, current activity is not confirmed); and precise like-for-like pricing against PiCar-X and ROSMASTER, since JetRacer's price swings heavily by bundle configuration in a way that resists a single clean number.

pricing.summary: Waveshare's own listings for the base AI Kit range from $213.99 to $632.99 depending on bundle configuration (with or without the Jetson Nano board, battery, and gamepad); the Pro AI Kit runs $255.99–$685.99, and the ROS Professional kit (adding an RPLiDAR A1 and IMU) runs $259.99–$694.99. Because so much of the price swings on which accessories are included, a fair comparison against other kits in this catalog requires checking exactly what's bundled, not just the headline number.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: JetRacer's onboard inference is genuinely GPU-accelerated rather than a marketing claim: training happens off-device in PyTorch, but inference runs optimized through TensorRT directly on the Jetson Nano's GPU — a real capability edge over CPU-only rival kits. Every JetRacer SKU depends on the now-EOL Jetson Nano, which NVIDIA is discontinuing with module support only through January 2027.

firmwareCommunity.note: Waveshare's own GitHub fork of NVIDIA's original open-source JetRacer project, adapted for its pre-assembled AI Kit hardware.
